headline: Application role gains unrestricted S3 access; a compromise now exposes entire data estate instead of specific buckets
suppressed: The PR author wants to avoid manual updates when analytics creates new buckets. This is a valid operational pain point, but the solution trades security for convenience. Better alternatives exist: use bucket name patterns (arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-*), tag-based access control, or automatic variable updates via CI/CD, each of which solves the real problem without exposing the entire S3 estate.

findings.evidence_ref: variables.tf line 30-31: app_data_bucket_arns default changed from specific bucket ARNs to ["*"]
findings.explanation: The application role now has read/write access to every S3 bucket in the account, not just acme-prod-data. Any compromise of the app grants attackers access to backups, logs, and sensitive data across the entire S3 estate.

findings.evidence_ref: variables.tf: removal of specific bucket ARN restrictions in favor of wildcard
findings.explanation: The guardrail limiting the app role to specific known buckets is being removed entirely. This is a permanent loosening of the security perimeter, not a temporary workaround for operational friction.
